title: Everything you think you know about addiction is wrong
speaker: Johann Hari

sentences.en: One of my earliest memories is of trying to wake up one of my relatives and not being able to.
sentences.zh: 我最早的记忆之一是试图叫醒我的一位亲戚，但没成功。

sentences.en: And I was just a little kid, so I didn't really understand why, but as I got older, I realized we had drug addiction in my family, including later cocaine addiction.
sentences.zh: 我当时只是个小孩子，所以我不太明白为什么，但随着年龄的增长，我意识到我们家里有毒瘾，包括后来的可卡因成瘾。

sentences.en: I'd been thinking about it a lot lately, partly because it's now exactly 100 years since drugs were first banned in the United States and Britain, and we then imposed that on the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 我最近一直在思考这个问题，部分原因是美国和英国首次禁止毒品已经整整 100 年了，然后我们又将这一禁令强加给世界其他国家。

sentences.en: It's a century since we made this really fateful decision to take addicts and punish them and make them suffer, because we believed that would deter them; it would give them an incentive to stop.
sentences.zh: 一个世纪以来，我们做出了这个决定性的决定，抓捕吸毒者并惩罚他们，让他们受苦，因为我们相信这会阻止他们；这会给他们停下来的动力。

sentences.en: And a few years ago, I was looking at some of the addicts in my life who I love, and trying to figure out if there was some way to help them.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我观察了生活中我所爱的一些瘾君子，并试图找出是否有某种方法可以帮助他们。

sentences.en: And I realized there were loads of incredibly basic questions I just didn't know the answer to, like, what really causes addiction?
sentences.zh: 我意识到有很多令人难以置信的基本问题我只是不知道答案，比如，真正导致成瘾的原因是什么？

sentences.en: Why do we carry on with this approach that doesn't seem to be working, and is there a better way out there that we could try instead?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们继续采用这种似乎行不通的方法？是否有更好的方法可以尝试？

sentences.en: So I read loads of stuff about it, and I couldn't really find the answers I was looking for, so I thought, okay, I'll go and sit with different people around the world who lived this and studied this and talk to them and see if I could learn from them.
sentences.zh: 所以我读了很多关于它的东西，但我无法真正找到我正在寻找的答案，所以我想，好吧，我会去和世界各地经历过这种情况并研究过这种情况的不同人坐在一起，与他们交谈，看看我是否可以向他们学习。

sentences.en: And I didn't realize I would end up going over 30,000 miles at the start, but I ended up going and meeting loads of different people, from a transgender crack dealer in Brownsville, Brooklyn, to a scientist who spends a lot of time feeding hallucinogens to mongooses
sentences.zh: 我没有意识到一开始我会行驶超过 30,000 英里，但我最终还是遇到了很多不同的人，从布鲁克林布朗斯维尔的变性强效毒品经销商，到花了很多时间给猫鼬喂致幻剂的科学家

sentences.en: to see if they like them -- it turns out they do, but only in very specific circumstances -- to the only country that's ever decriminalized all drugs, from cannabis to crack, Portugal.
sentences.zh: 看看他们是否喜欢它们——事实证明他们喜欢，但只是在非常特殊的情况下——到葡萄牙这个唯一一个将所有毒品（从大麻到强效毒品）合法化的国家。

sentences.en: And the thing I realized that really blew my mind is, almost everything we think we know about addiction is wrong, and if we start to absorb the new evidence about addiction, I think we're going to have to change a lot more than our drug policies.
sentences.zh: 我意识到真正让我大吃一惊的是，几乎我们认为我们所了解的有关成瘾的一切都是错误的，如果我们开始吸收有关成瘾的新证据，我认为我们将不得不改变的不仅仅是我们的毒品政策。

sentences.en: But let's start with what we think we know, what I thought I knew.
sentences.zh: 但让我们从我们认为我们知道的、我认为我知道的开始。

sentences.en: Let's think about this middle row here. Imagine all of you, for 20 days now, went off and used heroin three times a day.
sentences.zh: 让我们考虑一下中间这一行。想象一下，你们所有人在 20 天里每天吸食海洛因 3 次。

sentences.en: Some of you look a little more enthusiastic than others at this prospect.
sentences.zh: 对于这一前景，你们中的一些人看起来比其他人更热情一些。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Don't worry, it's just a thought experiment.
sentences.zh: （笑声）别担心，这只是一个思想实验。

sentences.en: Imagine you did that, right? What would happen?
sentences.zh: 想象一下你这样做了，对吗？会发生什么？

sentences.en: Now, we have a story about what would happen that we've been told for a century.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们有一个关于将会发生的事情的故事，我们已经被告知了一个世纪。

sentences.en: We think, because there are chemical hooks in heroin, as you took it for a while, your body would become dependent on those hooks, you'd start to physically need them, and at the end of those 20 days, you'd all be heroin addicts. Right?
sentences.zh: 我们认为，因为海洛因中含有化学钩子，当你服用一段时间后，你的身体就会对这些钩子产生依赖，你会开始身体上需要它们，在那20天结束时，你们都会成为海洛因成瘾者。正确的？

sentences.en: That's what I thought. First thing that alerted me to the fact that something's not right with this story is when it was explained to me.
sentences.zh: 我就是这么想的。首先让我意识到这个故事有问题的事实是当它向我解释时。

sentences.en: If I step out of this TED Talk today and I get hit by a car and I break my hip, I'll be taken to hospital and I'll be given loads of diamorphine.
sentences.zh: 如果我今天走出 TED 演讲，被车撞到，髋部骨折，我会被送往医院，并会被注射大量二吗啡。

sentences.en: Diamorphine is heroin. It's actually much better heroin than you're going to buy on the streets, because the stuff you buy from a drug dealer is contaminated.
sentences.zh: 二吗啡是海洛因。它实际上比你在街上买的海洛因好得多，因为你从毒贩那里买的东西已经被污染了。

sentences.en: Actually, very little of it is heroin, whereas the stuff you get from the doctor is medically pure.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中很少有海洛因，而你从医生那里得到的东西是纯医学的。

sentences.en: And you'll be given it for quite a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 而且你会在相当长的一段时间内得到它。

sentences.en: There are loads of people in this room, you may not realize it, you've taken quite a lot of heroin.
sentences.zh: 这个房间里有很多人，你可能没有意识到，你吸食了大量海洛因。

sentences.en: And anyone who is watching this anywhere in the world, this is happening.
sentences.zh: 任何在世界任何地方观看这一切的人，都会发现这种情况正在发生。

sentences.en: And if what we believe about addiction is right -- those people are exposed to all those chemical hooks -- What should happen? They should become addicts.
sentences.zh: 如果我们对成瘾的看法是正确的——那些人接触了所有这些化学物质——会发生什么？他们应该成为瘾君子。

sentences.en: This has been studied really carefully. It doesn't happen; you will have noticed if your grandmother had a hip replacement, she didn't come out as a junkie. (Laughter) And when I learned this, it seemed so weird to me, so contrary to everything I'd been told, everything I thought I knew,
sentences.zh: 这已经被非常仔细地研究过。它不会发生；你会注意到，如果你的祖母做了髋关节置换手术，她就不会成为瘾君子。 （笑声）当我了解到这一点时，我觉得这很奇怪，与我被告知的一切、我自以为知道的一切相反，

sentences.en: I just thought it couldn't be right, until I met a man called Bruce Alexander.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这不可能是对的，直到我遇到了一个叫布鲁斯·亚历山大的人。

sentences.en: He's a professor of psychology in Vancouver who carried out an incredible experiment I think really helps us to understand this issue.
sentences.zh: 他是温哥华的一位心理学教授，他进行了一项令人难以置信的实验，我认为这确实有助于我们理解这个问题。

sentences.en: Professor Alexander explained to me, the idea of addiction we've all got in our heads, that story, comes partly from a series of experiments that were done earlier in the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大教授向我解释说，我们脑子里都有的关于成瘾的想法，这个故事，部分来自于 20 世纪早期进行的一系列实验。

sentences.en: They're really simple. You can do them tonight at home if you feel a little sadistic.
sentences.zh: 它们真的很简单。如果你觉得有点虐待狂，你可以今晚在家做。

sentences.en: You get a rat and you put it in a cage, and you give it two water bottles: One is just water, and the other is water laced with either heroin or cocaine.
sentences.zh: 你把一只老鼠关在笼子里，然后给它两个水瓶：一个是水，另一个是掺有海洛因或可卡因的水。

sentences.en: If you do that, the rat will almost always prefer the drug water and almost always kill itself quite quickly.
sentences.zh: 如果你这样做，老鼠几乎总是更喜欢药水，并且几乎总是很快自杀。

sentences.en: So there you go, right? That's how we think it works.
sentences.zh: 那么就这样吧？我们认为这就是它的运作方式。

sentences.en: In the '70s, Professor Alexander comes along and he looks at this experiment and he noticed something.
sentences.zh: 七十年代，亚历山大教授出现，他观察了这个实验，并注意到了一些事情。

sentences.en: He said ah, we're putting the rat in an empty cage.
sentences.zh: 他说啊，我们要把老鼠关在空笼子里。

sentences.en: It's got nothing to do except use these drugs.
sentences.zh: 除了使用这些药物之外，没有任何事可做。

sentences.en: Let's try something different. So Professor Alexander built a cage that he called "Rat Park," which is basically heaven for rats.
sentences.zh: 让我们尝试一些不同的东西。因此亚历山大教授建造了一个他称之为“老鼠公园”的笼子，这基本上就是老鼠的天堂。

sentences.en: They've got loads of cheese, they've got loads of colored balls, they've got loads of tunnels.
sentences.zh: 他们有很多奶酪，有很多彩球，有很多隧道。

sentences.en: Crucially, they've got loads of friends. They can have loads of sex.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，他们有很多朋友。他们可以进行大量的性行为。

sentences.en: And they've got both the water bottles, the normal water and the drugged water.
sentences.zh: 他们有水瓶，普通水和加药水。

sentences.en: But here's the fascinating thing: In Rat Park, they don't like the drug water.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是：在老鼠公园，他们不喜欢药水。

sentences.en: They almost never use it. None of them ever use it compulsively.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎从不使用它。他们中没有人会强迫性地使用它。

sentences.en: None of them ever overdose. You go from almost 100 percent overdose when they're isolated to zero percent overdose when they have happy and connected lives.
sentences.zh: 他们中没有人服药过量。当他们被隔离时，几乎 100% 的药物过量，到当他们过着快乐且相互联系的生活时，药物过量为零。

sentences.en: Now, when he first saw this, Professor Alexander thought, maybe this is just a thing about rats, they're quite different to us.
sentences.zh: 现在，当亚历山大教授第一次看到这个时，他想，也许这只是老鼠的问题，它们与我们完全不同。

sentences.en: Maybe not as different as we'd like, but, you know -- But fortunately, there was a human experiment into the exact same principle happening at the exact same time.
sentences.zh: 也许没有我们想要的那么不同，但是，你知道——但幸运的是，在同一时间发生了一项针对完全相同原理的人体实验。

sentences.en: It was called the Vietnam War. In Vietnam, 20 percent of all American troops were using loads of heroin, and if you look at the news reports from the time, they were really worried, because they thought, my God, we're going to have
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的越南战争。在越南，20% 的美军使用了大量海洛因，如果你看看当时的新闻报道，他们真的很担心，因为他们认为，天啊，我们将会有

sentences.en: hundreds of thousands of junkies on the streets of the United States when the war ends; it made total sense.
sentences.zh: 战争结束后，美国街头有数十万吸毒者；这是完全有道理的。

sentences.en: Now, those soldiers who were using loads of heroin were followed home.
sentences.zh: 现在，那些吸食大量海洛因的士兵被跟踪回家。

sentences.en: The Archives of General Psychiatry did a really detailed study, and what happened to them?
sentences.zh: 普通精神病学档案馆做了非常详细的研究，他们发生了什么？

sentences.en: It turns out they didn't go to rehab. They didn't go into withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 事实证明他们没有去康复中心。他们没有进入戒断状态。

sentences.en: Ninety-five percent of them just stopped.
sentences.zh: 百分之九十五的人就停下来了。

sentences.en: Now, if you believe the story about chemical hooks, that makes absolutely no sense, but Professor Alexander began to think there might be a different story about addiction.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你相信有关化学钩子的故事，那绝对没有道理，但亚历山大教授开始认为关于成瘾可能有不同的故事。

sentences.en: He said, what if addiction isn't about your chemical hooks?
sentences.zh: 他说，如果成瘾与你的化学挂钩无关怎么办？

sentences.en: What if addiction is about your cage? What if addiction is an adaptation to your environment?
sentences.zh: 如果你的笼子上瘾怎么办？如果成瘾是对环境的适应怎么办？

sentences.en: Looking at this, there was another professor called Peter Cohen in the Netherlands who said, maybe we shouldn't even call it addiction.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这一点，荷兰另一位名叫彼得·科恩的教授说，也许我们甚至不应该称之为成瘾。

sentences.en: Maybe we should call it bonding. Human beings have a natural and innate need to bond, and when we're happy and healthy, we'll bond and connect with each other, but if you can't do that, because you're traumatized or isolated or beaten down by life,
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该称其为粘合。人类有一种天生的、与生俱来的联系需求，当我们快乐和健康时，我们会彼此联系和联系，但如果你不能这样做，因为你受到了创伤、孤立或被生活击垮，

sentences.en: you will bond with something that will give you some sense of relief.
sentences.zh: 你会与一些能给你带来解脱感的事物联系在一起。

sentences.en: Now, that might be gambling, that might be pornography, that might be cocaine, that might be cannabis, but you will bond and connect with something because that's our nature.
sentences.zh: 现在，这可能是赌博，可能是色情，可能是可卡因，可能是大麻，但你会与某些东西产生联系，因为这是我们的本性。

sentences.en: That's what we want as human beings. And at first, I found this quite a difficult thing to get my head around, but one way that helped me to think about it is, I can see, I've got over by my seat a bottle of water, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是我们作为人类想要的。起初，我发现这是一件很难让我头脑清醒的事情，但帮助我思考这个问题的一个方法是，我可以看到，我在座位旁边放了一瓶水，对吗？

sentences.en: I'm looking at lots of you, and lots of you have bottles of water with you.
sentences.zh: 我看着你们很多人，很多人都带着瓶装水。

sentences.en: Forget the drugs. Forget the drug war. Totally legally, all of those bottles of water could be bottles of vodka, right?
sentences.zh: 忘记毒品吧。忘记毒品战争吧。完全合法，所有这些瓶装水都可以是伏特加瓶，对吧？

sentences.en: We could all be getting drunk -- I might after this -- (Laughter) -- but we're not.
sentences.zh: 我们都可能会喝醉——我可能会在这之后——（笑声）——但我们没有。

sentences.en: Now, because you've been able to afford the approximately gazillion pounds that it costs to get into a TED Talk, I'm guessing you guys could afford to be drinking vodka for the next six months.
sentences.zh: 现在，因为你们已经能够承担参加 TED 演讲所需的大约数亿英镑的费用，所以我猜你们在接下来的六个月里可以喝得起伏特加。

sentences.en: You wouldn't end up homeless. You're not going to do that, and the reason you're not going to do that is not because anyone's stopping you.
sentences.zh: 你不会最终无家可归。你不会那样做，你不会那样做的原因并不是因为有人阻止你。

sentences.en: It's because you've got bonds and connections that you want to be present for.
sentences.zh: 这是因为你已经拥有了你想要出席的纽带和联系。

sentences.en: You've got work you love. You've got people you love.
sentences.zh: 你有你热爱的工作。你有你爱的人。

sentences.en: You've got healthy relationships. And a core part of addiction, I came to think, and I believe the evidence suggests, is about not being able to bear to be present in your life.
sentences.zh: 你拥有健康的人际关系。我开始认为，而且我相信证据表明，成瘾的核心部分是无法忍受出现在你的生活中。

sentences.en: Now, this has really significant implications.
sentences.zh: 现在，这具有非常重大的意义。

sentences.en: The most obvious implications are for the War on Drugs.
sentences.zh: 最明显的影响是对毒品战争的影响。

sentences.en: In Arizona, I went out with a group of women who were made to wear t-shirts saying, "I was a drug addict," and go out on chain gangs and dig graves while members of the public jeer at them,
sentences.zh: 在亚利桑那州，我和一群妇女出去，她们被迫穿着 T 恤，上面写着“我是个吸毒者”，然后带着铁链出去挖坟墓，而公众却嘲笑她们，

sentences.en: and when those women get out of prison, they're going to have criminal records that mean they'll never work in the legal economy again.
sentences.zh: 当这些女性出狱后，她们将有犯罪记录，这意味着她们将永远无法再在合法经济中工作。

sentences.en: Now, that's a very extreme example, obviously, in the case of the chain gang, but actually almost everywhere in the world we treat addicts to some degree like that.
sentences.zh: 显然，就铁链团伙而言，这是一个非常极端的例子，但实际上世界上几乎所有地方我们都在某种程度上以同样的方式对待瘾君子。

sentences.en: We punish them. We shame them. We give them criminal records.
sentences.zh: 我们惩罚他们。我们羞辱他们。我们向他们提供犯罪记录。

sentences.en: We put barriers between them reconnecting.
sentences.zh: 我们在他们重新连接之间设置了障碍。

sentences.en: There was a doctor in Canada, Dr. Gabor Maté, an amazing man, who said to me, if you wanted to design a system that would make addiction worse, you would design that system.
sentences.zh: 加拿大有一位医生，Gabor Maté 博士，他是一位了不起的人，他对我说，如果你想设计一个让成瘾变得更糟的系统，你就设计那个系统。

sentences.en: Now, there's a place that decided to do the exact opposite, and I went there to see how it worked.
sentences.zh: 现在，有一个地方决定采取完全相反的做法，我去那里看看它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: In the year 2000, Portugal had one of the worst drug problems in Europe.
sentences.zh: 2000年，葡萄牙是欧洲毒品问题最严重的国家之一。

sentences.en: One percent of the population was addicted to heroin, which is kind of mind-blowing, and every year, they tried the American way more and more.
sentences.zh: 百分之一的人口对海洛因上瘾，这有点令人兴奋，而且每年他们都越来越多地尝试美国的方式。

sentences.en: They punished people and stigmatized them and shamed them more, and every year, the problem got worse.
sentences.zh: 他们惩罚人们、污蔑他们、羞辱他们，而且问题一年比一年严重。

sentences.en: And one day, the Prime Minister and the leader of the opposition got together, and basically said, look, we can't go on with a country where we're having ever more people becoming heroin addicts.
sentences.zh: 有一天，首相和反对派领导人聚在一起，基本上说，看，我们不能再继续这样一个国家，越来越多的人成为海洛因成瘾者。

sentences.en: Let's set up a panel of scientists and doctors to figure out what would genuinely solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 让我们成立一个由科学家和医生组成的小组来找出真正解决问题的方法。

sentences.en: And they set up a panel led by an amazing man called Dr. João Goulão, to look at all this new evidence, and they came back and they said, "Decriminalize all drugs from cannabis to crack, but" -- and this is the crucial next step --
sentences.zh: 他们成立了一个由 João Goulão 博士领导的小组来研究所有这些新证据，他们回来后说，“将大麻等所有毒品合法化，但是”——这是下一步至关重要的——

sentences.en: "take all the money we used to spend on cutting addicts off, on disconnecting them, and spend it instead on reconnecting them with society."
sentences.zh: “把我们过去花在与成瘾者断绝关系、与他们断绝关系上所花的所有钱，花在让他们与社会重新建立联系上。”

sentences.en: And that's not really what we think of as drug treatment in the United States and Britain.
sentences.zh: 在美国和英国，这并不是我们所认为的药物治疗。

sentences.en: So they do residential rehab, they do psychological therapy, that does have some value.
sentences.zh: 所以他们进行住院康复治疗，进行心理治疗，这确实有一定的价值。

sentences.en: But the biggest thing they did was the complete opposite of what we do: a massive program of job creation for addicts, and microloans for addicts to set up small businesses.
sentences.zh: 但他们所做的最重要的事情与我们所做的完全相反：为吸毒者创造就业机会的大规模计划，以及为吸毒者提供小额贷款来创办小企业。

sentences.en: So say you used to be a mechanic. When you're ready, they'll go to a garage, and they'll say, if you employ this guy for a year, we'll pay half his wages.
sentences.zh: 假设你曾经是一名机械师。当你准备好后，他们会去车库，他们会说，如果你雇用这个人一年，我们将支付他一半的工资。

sentences.en: The goal was to make sure that every addict in Portugal had something to get out of bed for in the morning.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标是确保葡萄牙的每个瘾君子早上都有东西可以起床。

sentences.en: And when I went and met the addicts in Portugal, what they said is, as they rediscovered purpose, they rediscovered bonds and relationships with the wider society.
sentences.zh: 当我去葡萄牙见到瘾君子时，他们说，当他们重新发现目标时，他们重新发现了与更广泛社会的联系和关系。

sentences.en: It'll be 15 years this year since that experiment began, and the results are in: injecting drug use is down in Portugal, according to the British Journal of Criminology, by 50 percent, five-zero percent.
sentences.zh: 今年距离该实验开始已有 15 年了，结果如下：根据《英国犯罪学杂志》的报道，葡萄牙的注射毒品使用率下降了 50%、5-0%。

sentences.en: Overdose is massively down, HIV is massively down among addicts.
sentences.zh: 吸毒过量现象大幅减少，成瘾者中的艾滋病毒感染率也大幅下降。

sentences.en: Addiction in every study is significantly down.
sentences.zh: 每项研究中的成瘾率均显着下降。

sentences.en: One of the ways you know it's worked so well is that almost nobody in Portugal wants to go back to the old system.
sentences.zh: 你知道它运作良好的原因之一是，葡萄牙几乎没有人愿意回到旧系统。

sentences.en: Now, that's the political implications. I actually think there's a layer of implications to all this research below that.
sentences.zh: 现在，这就是政治影响。事实上，我认为所有这些研究都有一层含义。

sentences.en: We live in a culture where people feel really increasingly vulnerable to all sorts of addictions, whether it's to their smartphones or to shopping or to eating.
sentences.zh: 在我们生活的文化中，人们越来越容易沉迷于各种沉迷，无论是对智能手机、购物还是饮食。

sentences.en: Before these talks began -- you guys know this -- we were told we weren't allowed to have our smartphones on, and I have to say, a lot of you looked an awful lot like addicts who were told their dealer was going to be unavailable
sentences.zh: 在这些会谈开始之前——你们知道这一点——我们被告知我们不可以打开我们的智能手机，我不得不说，你们中的很多人看起来非常像瘾君子，他们被告知他们的经销商将无法联系。

sentences.en: for the next couple of hours. (Laughter) A lot of us feel like that, and it might sound weird to say, I've been talking about how disconnection is a major driver of addiction and weird to say it's growing, because you think we're the most connected society that's ever been, surely.
sentences.zh: 接下来的几个小时。 （笑声）我们很多人都有这样的感觉，这听起来可能很奇怪，我一直在谈论断线是如何成为成瘾的主要驱动因素，而且说它正在增长也很奇怪，因为你认为我们是有史以来联系最紧密的社会，当然。

sentences.en: But I increasingly began to think that the connections we have or think we have, are like a kind of parody of human connection.
sentences.zh: 但我越来越开始认为，我们拥有的或认为我们拥有的联系就像是对人类联系的一种模仿。

sentences.en: If you have a crisis in your life, you'll notice something.
sentences.zh: 如果你的生活遇到危机，你会注意到一些事情。

sentences.en: It won't be your Twitter followers who come to sit with you.
sentences.zh: 不会是你的推特追随者来跟你坐在一起

sentences.en: It won't be your Facebook friends who help you turn it round.
sentences.zh: 不会是你脸书上的朋友帮你转过身来

sentences.en: It'll be your flesh and blood friends who you have deep and nuanced and textured, face-to-face relationships with, and there's a study I learned about from Bill McKibben, the environmental writer, that I think tells us a lot about this.
sentences.zh: 和你的血肉朋友们 你和他们有着深厚的 细细的 纹理的 面对面的关系 我从比尔・麦基本那里学到了

sentences.en: It looked at the number of close friends the average American believes they can call on in a crisis.
sentences.zh: 调查了普通美国人认为 在危机中他们可以求助的亲密朋友的数量。

sentences.en: That number has been declining steadily since the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 自1950年代以来,这一数字一直在稳步下降。

sentences.en: The amount of floor space an individual has in their home has been steadily increasing, and I think that's like a metaphor for the choice we've made as a culture.
sentences.zh: 一个人在家里的楼层空间 一直在稳步增加, 我认为这就像一个比喻 我们作为一个文化所作的选择。

sentences.en: We've traded floorspace for friends, we've traded stuff for connections, and the result is we are one of the loneliest societies there has ever been.
sentences.zh: 我们把楼层空间换成朋友, 把东西换成连接, 结果我们是最孤独的社会之一。

sentences.en: And Bruce Alexander, the guy who did the Rat Park experiment, says, we talk all the time in addiction about individual recovery, and it's right to talk about that, but we need to talk much more about social recovery.
sentences.zh: 和布鲁斯亚历山大, 做鼠公园实验的人, 说,我们一直在谈论 上瘾 关于个人康复, 这是正确的谈论, 但我们需要谈论更多 关于社会康复。

sentences.en: Something's gone wrong with us, not just with individuals but as a group, and we've created a society where, for a lot of us, life looks a whole lot more like that isolated cage and a whole lot less like Rat Park.
sentences.zh: 我们之间出了点问题, 不只是个人之间,而是作为一个群体, 我们创造了一个社会, 对许多人来说,生活看起来 更像是那个孤立的笼子, 更不像老鼠公园。

sentences.en: If I'm honest, this isn't why I went into it.
sentences.zh: 如果我是诚实的,这不是为什么我进入它。

sentences.en: I didn't go in to the discover the political stuff, the social stuff.
sentences.zh: 我没有去 发现政治的东西, 社会的东西。

sentences.en: I wanted to know how to help the people I love.
sentences.zh: 我想知道如何帮助我爱的人

sentences.en: And when I came back from this long journey and I'd learned all this, I looked at the addicts in my life, and if you're really candid, it's hard loving an addict, and there's going to be lots of people who know in this room.
sentences.zh: 当我从这漫长的旅程回来 学到了这一切, 我看着我的生活中的瘾君子, 如果你真的坦率, 这是很难爱上一个瘾君子,

sentences.en: You are angry a lot of the time, and I think one of the reasons why this debate is so charged is because it runs through the heart of each of us, right?
sentences.zh: 你经常生气 我想这次辩论之所以如此激烈的原因之一 是因为它贯穿了我们每个人的心 对不对?

sentences.en: Everyone has a bit of them that looks at an addict and thinks, I wish someone would just stop you.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有一点点 他们看着一个瘾君子 并思考, 我希望有人会 只是阻止你。

sentences.en: And the kind of scripts we're told for how to deal with the addicts in our lives is typified by, I think, the reality show "Intervention," if you guys have ever seen it.
sentences.zh: 而我们被告知如何对付我们生活中的瘾君子的剧本 典型的就是真实节目“Intervention”,如果你们见过的话。

sentences.en: I think everything in our lives is defined by reality TV, but that's another TED Talk.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们生活中的一切都是由现实电视来定义的, 但是这是另一场TED演讲。

sentences.en: If you've ever seen the show "Intervention," it's a pretty simple premise.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过"干预"的节目, 这是一个很简单的前提。

sentences.en: Get an addict, all the people in their life, gather them together, confront them with what they're doing, and they say, if you don't shape up, we're going to cut you off.
sentences.zh: 去找个瘾君子 把他们聚在一起 面对他们正在做的事 他们说 如果你不振作起来 我们就把你切下来

sentences.en: So what they do is they take the connection to the addict, and they threaten it, they make it contingent on the addict behaving the way they want.
sentences.zh: 所以他们做的是 与瘾君子的联系, 他们威胁它, 他们让它 取决于瘾君子 行为的方式,他们想要的。

sentences.en: And I began to think, I began to see why that approach doesn't work, and I began to think that's almost like the importing of the logic of the Drug War into our private lives.
sentences.zh: 我开始思考,我开始理解为什么这个方法不起作用, 我开始认为这几乎就像 药物战争的逻辑输入到我们的私人生活中。

sentences.en: So I was thinking, how could I be Portuguese?
sentences.zh: 所以我在想,我怎么会是葡萄牙人?

sentences.en: And what I've tried to do now, and I can't tell you I do it consistently and I can't tell you it's easy, is to say to the addicts in my life that I want to deepen the connection with them, to say to them, I love you whether you're using or you're not.
sentences.zh: 我试图做的, 我不能告诉你我一直这样做, 我不能告诉你这很容易, 是对我的生活中的瘾君子说, 我想加深与他们的联系, 对他们说,我爱你 不管你在用与否。

sentences.en: I love you, whatever state you're in, and if you need me, I'll come and sit with you because I love you and I don't want you to be alone or to feel alone.
sentences.zh: 我爱你 无论你身处什么状态 如果你需要我 我会跟你坐在一起 因为我爱你

sentences.en: And I think the core of that message -- you're not alone, we love you -- has to be at every level of how we respond to addicts, socially, politically and individually.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个信息的核心 -- 你并不孤单,我们爱你 -- 必须是我们如何应对吸毒成瘾者, 社会、政治和个人。

sentences.en: For 100 years now, we've been singing war songs about addicts.
sentences.zh: 100年来 我们一直在唱关于瘾君子的战争歌曲

sentences.en: I think all along we should have been singing love songs to them, because the opposite of addiction is not sobriety.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们应该一直 唱情歌给他们, 因为反 成瘾不是清醒。

sentences.en: The opposite of addiction is connection.
sentences.zh: 与吸毒成瘾相反的是关联。

sentences.en: Thank you. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 谢谢。 （掌声）
